subject: DPA questions: operator telemetry, BYOK escrow options, and cross-border controls
messages:
From: Sarah Barnes <sarah.barnes@nimbushealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions re: private deployment (BYOK + operator access)

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we get into procurement, our legal and security teams asked for clarity on three items specific to a private deployment (VPC/on-prem):

1) Operator access profile — what telemetry/ops data Redwood collects from a private deployment, and whether operator access can be strictly ephemeral and logged.
2) BYOK: do you require key escrow for private deployments or is customer-only custody supported end-to-end? Any options or addenda we should expect?
3) Cross-border telemetry / metrics routing — we need assurance that any logs or monitoring data for Nimbus accounts resident in the EU will not transit to non-EU jurisdictions.

I attached a short spreadsheet with our legal team's questions (nimbus_dpa_questions.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to specific DPA language or provide an annex we can review?

Appreciate it — would like to keep this moving this week.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Barnes
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Barnes <sarah.barnes@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: private deployment (BYOK + operator access)

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending these through and for the clear list. I've skimmed the spreadsheet and included our privacy/ops leads in the thread to scope the right annex language. High-level answers up front:

- Operator access: For Private (VPC/on-prem) we support strictly ephemeral operator sessions instrumented by jump-hosts and MFA; we can include acceptance criteria in an annex around scope, duration, and auditing (session audit logs retained per your retention policy).
- BYOK: Customer-only custody is supported. We do not mandate escrow as a baseline; escrow is an optional addendum for customers who require it, and it carries specific legal/ops controls (we can provide sample language).
- Telemetry routing: We can configure telemetry endpoints to keep monitoring data within a given region (EU) and we have options to scrub PII from diagnostic traces before any telemetry leaves the VPC.

Irene/Grace — can you confirm the default retention window for operator session logs and whether we have a hardened routing config to ensure EU-only telemetry endpoints? Also, is there a standard annex PDF we can send to Nimbus?

Sarah — I'll follow up with a draft annex and two options for the BYOK section (no-escrow default + optional escrow addendum) by EOD.

Cheers,
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Nimbus DPA items — operator audit windows & telemetry routing

Lukas — internal notes:

- Operator logs: default retention 90 days, can be shortened to 30 days on request; we can add language to DPA stating "operator session logs retained for X days unless contractually modified."
- Telemetry routing: we have a config for region-locked telemetry using private collectors (EU collectors) for Private deploys; we need ops to commit to hard network-level egress rules (no fallback to global collectors). Grace, can you confirm the deployment playbook change to lock collectors to EU?
- BYOK escrow: standard practice is customer-only keys with optional escrow. Escrow option adds: (a) dual-control access policy, (b) escrow key split across two escrow holders, (c) explicit trigger events for retrieval. Note that escrow requires SOC2 + additional contractual controls — ops cost and lead time need to be surfaced.

I'll draft a short annex text for the operator access paragraph and share before EOD.

—Irene

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sarah Barnes <sarah.barnes@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: private deployment (BYOK + operator access)

Hi Sarah and team — looping in directly with a proposed annex (attached) that addresses your three items and includes two BYOK variants: "Customer-Only Custody" and "Optional Escrow". Summary of key points in the annex:

- Operator Access: Redwood operator access to private deployments is limited to ephemeral, MFA-guarded sessions; each session is logged (session start/end, operator id, commands executed) and logs are exportable to customer SIEM. Default retention: 90 days; negotiable.
- Telemetry/Logs: Diagnostic telemetry and metrics can be routed to EU-only collectors. We will include a contractual obligation to prevent automatic routing to non-EU collectors and to scrub PII from traces prior to export.
- BYOK: Default is no escrow — customer retains sole custody. If Nimbus requests escrow, the annex includes escrow governance (split-escrow, dual-approval retrieval, and annual escrow tests). Escrow incurs additional procurement workstreams (legal + ops) and timeline impact (~6–8 weeks).

Attachments: redwood_privdep_annex_v1.pdf (draft annex), summary table embedded in the PDF.

Next steps: If this looks reasonable, we'll issue a DocuSign for the annex and the DPA addendum and provide a short operational playbook for your engineers describing the EU-collector config.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Barnes <sarah.barnes@nimbushealth.com>

Subject: Re: DPA questions re: private deployment (BYOK + operator access)

Thanks Grace — quick clarifications from legal: 

1) For operator session logs, can you accept a 30-day default with an option to extend to 90 days if we request it? Our baseline is short retention.
2) On the escrow timeline — the 6–8 week impact is acceptable but we need to know cost delta and an initial list of escrow holders (can be Redwood-managed but preferred: third-party escrow).

If you can add a short paragraph to the annex covering point (1) and a line item estimating the additional procurement/Ops cost for escrow, we can circulate internally and get back to you. 

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sarah
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Barnes <sarah.barnes@nimbushealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: private deployment (BYOK + operator access)

Sarah — quick operational confirmation:

- We can make 30 days the default retention for operator session logs and include a customer option to extend to 90 days (we'll put exact language into the annex).
- Escrow cost delta: approximate one-time setup and governance fee of $18k–$28k depending on escrow provider and split-holder setup; ongoing annual maintenance $3k–$5k. We will provide a formal estimate if you decide to proceed.
- Escrow holders: we recommend a neutral third-party escrow provider (we've used KeySafe Solutions previously) or a split model with an internal Redwood key custodian + third-party escrow. Full options included in the annex.

I'll attach the updated annex with the 30/90 day retention clause and a placeholder cost table after this message.

—Rishi
